set-screw-tip-selection:
Compare the four contact mechanisms

Set-screw point selection: geometry and trade-offs
Point formContactWhen to review itWhat to verify
Flat pointA broad end face bears against a prepared flat or pad.Review for adjustments where a sharp biting edge is undesirable.It can still mark the mating surface. Check flat alignment, contact pressure and retention.
Cone pointA pointed end engages a suitable recess or indents the mating surface.Review for a defined setting where penetration or a mating recess is acceptable.Repeated relocation can damage the contact area. Define the cone and the mating feature.
Dog pointA cylindrical extension enters a prepared hole or slot.Review when the extension must locate or guide a component.Specify projection, diameter, clearance and available depth; do not let the point bottom unintentionally.
Cup pointThe rim of a recessed end makes concentrated contact.Review for a setting where an indentation is acceptable.Do not assume an undamaged surface after removal, or infer a universal holding force from the point name.

Compare the contact mechanism first; confirm capacity and installation on the actual joint.

Shoulder-screw inspection-plan example
CharacteristicRequirement to enterSuitable evidenceCoverage and record
C1 · Shoulder diameterApproved drawing limits; final supplied conditionCalibrated diameter measurement; validated vision only if suitableAgreed sample or every-piece scope; record actual values or the approved screening result
C2 · Shoulder lengthDistance from the functional seating faceLength measurement from the specified face, with a documented setupLink the result to the drawing revision and lot
C3 · Thread acceptanceThread system, pitch, class and usable lengthAppropriate gauges plus a separate usable-length check when requiredRecord gauge identity and the agreed acceptance result
C4 · Geometric runout, if specifiedDatum, controlled surface and tolerance on the drawingA datum-referenced setup that measures the specified relationshipA diameter-only camera result does not replace this check
C5 · Material and finishOrdered grade, condition and treatment requirementsAgreed documents and applicable physical or coating checksKeep stock certificates, final-part results and coating records distinguishable
C6 · Assembly functionApproved mating-part revision and functional criteriaControlled assembly trial for movement, seating or retentionRecord the mating reference, outcome, deviations and approver
